$comment: Test fixture consumed by crates/gateway/tests/t20_reference_parity.rs. Authoritative copy lives in quotio-rs docs/reference/provider-parity-deviations.json - re-sync from that source after changes. The `behavioralDeviations` array is audit-owned (2026-11-08 provider-parity audit) and is not consumed by t20_reference_parity.rs; it records deliberate relay/streaming differences that are not registry fields. A provider path with no counterpart in either reference is never claimed as parity: Meta Muse (L6-D4) is recorded here, and Zcode/OpenCode provider contracts are marked NOT-CERTIFIED in .omo/evidence/provider-parity-audit/defects.md.
note: Deliberate differences between the OpenCodex provider registry snapshot and Quotio's provider catalog. An omission is a reference provider Quotio deliberately does not expose. Every entry is enforced: an undeclared difference fails provider-catalog.test.ts, and a declared difference that no longer exists fails it too. An omitted provider must be absent from the catalog and from the parity manifest.

deviations.reason: Quotio onboards Kiro by importing an existing credential (crates/gateway/src/management/creds.rs) instead of driving a browser OAuth round trip. The reference flow (opencodex/src/oauth/kiro.ts) also reads a local credential file, so the imported shape is identical; only the entry point differs.

The reference label distinguishes two onboarding modes in its own picker. Quotio exposes a single Command Code entry whose OAuth callback lifecycle is implemented, so the mode suffix would be misleading in this UI.

behavioralDeviations.behavior: count_tokens is a documented local bytes/4 approximation; tools and images contribute no tokens.
behavioralDeviations.reason: Upstream token counting is not exposed to the proxy; the approximation is documented at the call site and never presented as an exact count.

behavioralDeviations.behavior: JSON response formats are rejected unless the catalog advertises a native capability.
behavioralDeviations.reason: The reference synthesises output_config.format, which is outside our declared capability contract; we refuse instead of silently substituting.

behavioralDeviations.behavior: Later system/developer turns stay in history as user messages.
behavioralDeviations.reason: Hoisting them to the system block rewrites the cached prefix; we keep prefix stability and document the tradeoff.

behavioralDeviations.behavior: The aistudio provider represents connected WebSocket workers; direct Google API-key traffic lives in the generic adapter=google path.
behavioralDeviations.reason: Different transport, different credential shape; conflating them would invent a provider identity.

behavioralDeviations.behavior: max_tokens/max_completion_tokens are dropped for Codex destinations.
behavioralDeviations.reason: Live Codex rejects the budget field; opencodex strips it too. The references disagree with each other, so this is a destination-specific policy.

behavioralDeviations.behavior: StrictRoundRobin keys on a member-id service sequence, not a previous-picked-identity cursor.
behavioralDeviations.reason: Both resist positional cursor churn; ours is documented as a contract in docs/CONTRACTS.md.

behavioralDeviations.behavior: Claude subscription slots rank by earliest weekly reset, with nearly-spent new-session accounts last.
behavioralDeviations.reason: A ranks generic failover by measured headroom; ours is a documented cache-preserving policy, not a payload difference.

behavioralDeviations.behavior: Chat keepalive emits a full chat chunk with a role prelude and empty delta.
behavioralDeviations.reason: Client-specific liveness; both are complete SSE frames, never mid-line insertions.

behavioralDeviations.behavior: Devin is exposed as an experimental local integration.
behavioralDeviations.reason: Declared experimental; absence from the reference registry is not a defect.

behavioralDeviations.behavior: Local exec is the default: with MAHOQUOT_EXEC_BRIDGE unset the gateway executes cursor exec requests on its own host (a one-time warning on stderr), and MAHOQUOT_EXEC_ROOT defaults to / (compat/cursor.rs:1329-1334). Paths are still contained by .. rejection (exec_write_rejects_dotdot_escape).
behavioralDeviations.reason: The reference runs exec on the operator's own machine. A standalone gateway has no such machine, so the documented behaviour is explicit local execution rather than an implicit fallback; operators who need isolation set MAHOQUOT_EXEC_BRIDGE or MAHOQUOT_EXEC_ROOT.

behavioralDeviations.reference: CLIProxyAPI zcode plugin (plan vs api host selected per model family)
behavioralDeviations.behavior: The plan identity is applied per model family so a plan-scoped model is never sent to the api host and vice versa.
behavioralDeviations.reason: The reference exposes separate hosts per family without a shared identity model; applying identity per family preserves routed model semantics without rewriting the client's model name.

behavioralDeviations.behavior: An OpenCode model is allowed only when the pinned opencodex registry snapshot lists it.
behavioralDeviations.reason: The catalog is the contract for which OpenCode models exist; admitting models the snapshot does not list invents capability the provider may not serve.

behavioralDeviations.reference: none: neither opencodex nor CLIProxyAPI implements the first-party Meta Muse device-authorization or muse-code wire
behavioralDeviations.behavior: Muse onboarding uses OIDC device authorization, a DCA-to-API-key mint, and pinned muse-code / muse-build user agents; inference is Responses SSE on /responses.
behavioralDeviations.reason: Muse is a first-party provider added here by product requirement. There is no reference implementation to compare against, so this path is declared as an uncompared deviation instead of being claimed as parity.
